note: Gameplay tuning: building catalog for City View slots. Track bases for farm, workshop, depot and fort are in logistics_tuning.json development; every level's cost and upkeep is the base times cost_multiplier_pct for that level.
demolish_note: Salvage only (timber, nails, brick sold off), not a refund.
cost_note: Level 1, 2 and 3 cost x1, x2.5 and x6 of the base, and a building's upkeep rises in the same steps.

powder_purchase.note: Powder is imported: it can be bought only into a town that has this building and one of these tags.

buildings.name: Farm
buildings.campaign_effect: Each level: +3 provisions a month here and a larger town levy (monthly ledger).
buildings.battle_effect: The town's holder: readiness +2 a level, reinforcements 5% faster (card: Readiness, Reinforcements).
buildings.description: Fields and barns that feed the magazine and steady the muster.

buildings.name: Workshop
buildings.campaign_effect: Each level: +1 musket a month here (monthly ledger); faster cartridge making.
buildings.battle_effect: The town's holder: +8 cartridges a level, so more rounds a man (card: Rounds a man).
buildings.description: A flintlock shop that turns powder, lead and paper into cartridges.

buildings.name: Depot
buildings.campaign_effect: Shipments arrive sooner. At a harbour or crossroads: +8 gold a month a level (monthly ledger). At a harbour: lets you buy powder.
buildings.battle_effect: The town's holder: readiness +2 a level, reinforcements 5% faster (card: Readiness, Reinforcements).
buildings.description: Storehouse and wagons for powder, provisions and arms.

buildings.name: Fort
buildings.campaign_effect: Lets the town enlist provincial regulars. A garrison beaten here is besieged 72 hours a level before the town falls.
buildings.battle_effect: The defender starts holding a post: morale +3 and readiness +2 a level, extra cover (card: Fortification, Morale, Readiness).
buildings.description: Earthworks and palisades that stiffen the defense.

buildings.name: Powder Mill
buildings.campaign_effect: Each level: +2 powder a month here (monthly ledger).
buildings.battle_effect: Powder here is made up into cartridges, 10 a powder: more rounds a man (card: Rounds a man).
buildings.description: A stamping mill on running water that makes gunpowder.

buildings.name: Meeting House
buildings.campaign_effect: +5 Support when built; +1 Support a month (monthly ledger).
buildings.description: The parish meeting house that steadies local Support.

buildings.name: Militia Muster
buildings.campaign_effect: Lets the town raise militia companies.
buildings.battle_effect: More militia companies march in for the defender (card: Militia muster).
buildings.description: Drill ground where minutemen form and march to the posts.

recruit_note: GAME INVENTION. One company musters per town at a time; men come from the town's monthly manpower (base below at Support 50, scaled by Support 25-100). Militia and riflemen bring their own firelocks; regulars are armed from the town magazine. 'faction' limits who may raise a company (empty = anyone); 'requires_chapter' holds it back until that campaign chapter (continental = Congress adopts the army, 14 June 1775, the day it voted the first rifle companies). 'role' is the battlefield summary shown to the player; the battle values themselves live in the Unreal class kits.
economy_note: GAME INVENTION. Settled on the 1st of each month: levies, depot trade and workshop muskets in; army pay, building upkeep and loan interest out. A shortfall is borrowed up to credit_per_town x towns held; past that the army goes unpaid. Retuned in Phase 4 so that a level-1 building costs about two months of the opening net income (levy 15 -> 4 a supply point, regular pay 2 -> 3; the sea subsidy rose 80 -> 135, which leaves the British accounts where they stood: +3 gold a month at the opening). 2026-11-14: the Boston garrison opens with 4 gun crews (regular pay 12), so the subsidy rose 135 -> 147 to keep that +3.
enemy_economy_note: GAME INVENTION. The other side settles the same accounts from its own war chest (starts at 60, never shown). A side that controls the harbour and holds its headquarters town also lands sea_subsidy_gold and sea_provisions each month. It cannot borrow: unpaid means -unpaid_morale. With gold above enemy_reserve_gold it raises its cheapest available company once a month.

recruits.name: Militia company
recruits.role: Skirmishers. Shoot best from walls and fences; unsteady in the open; no bayonets.
recruits.description: Townsmen who turn out with their own firelocks.

recruits.name: Provincial regulars
recruits.role: Line infantry. Stand in ranks and fire volleys; steadier than militia; a few bayonets.
recruits.description: Enlisted men drilled in the works and armed from the magazine.

recruits.name: Rifle company
recruits.role: Marksmen. Long rifles hit at twice a musket's range but load slowly; no bayonet, weak hand to hand.
recruits.description: Frontier riflemen with their own long rifles, voted by Congress on 14 June 1775.

recruits.name: Company officer
recruits.role: Leader. Men within 15 m of him aim steadier and load faster. Carries a light fusil.
recruits.description: A captain or lieutenant to steady the men and order their fire.

recruits.name: Company of foot
recruits.role: Line infantry. Crisp volleys in the open and the bayonet to follow.
recruits.description: A battalion company of a regiment of foot.

recruits.name: Grenadier company
recruits.role: Shock troops. The tallest, strongest men: hardest to kill and deadliest with the bayonet.
recruits.description: The regiment's right-flank company, picked for size and steadiness.

recruits.name: Light infantry company
recruits.role: Skirmishers. Fast in loose order, use cover, fire at will; lighter in a bayonet fight.
recruits.description: The regiment's left-flank company, picked for agility and marksmanship.

recruits.name: Troop of light horse
recruits.role: Dragoons (GAME INVENTION for 1775). Ride to the fight, dismount out of musket range and fight on foot with carbines; remount to move. No bayonet.
recruits.description: Farmers' sons on their own horses, mounted from the town's farms and armed from the magazine.

recruits.name: Troop of light dragoons
recruits.role: Dragoons (GAME INVENTION for 1775). Ride to the fight, dismount out of musket range and fight on foot with carbines; remount to move. No bayonet.
recruits.description: A troop of light dragoons with their carbines, pistols and sabres.

recruits.name: Party of sappers
recruits.role: Field works: in battle they build and mend breastworks at the places marked for them, on ground your side holds.
recruits.description: Men with spades and axes, raised where a Fort gives them officers who know the work.

recruits.name: Party of pioneers
recruits.role: Field works: in battle they build and mend breastworks at the places marked for them, on ground their side holds.
recruits.description: The regiment's pioneers with their axes, saws and spades.

recruits.name: Colour party
recruits.role: Carries the colours in battle: squads near them rally in half the time; if they fall the whole side feels it, and colours taken raise or lower Support.
recruits.description: An ensign and his guard with the regiment's colour.

recruits.name: Fifes and drums
recruits.role: Signals in battle: an order carries on through them, and line infantry near them load in cadence.

recruits.name: Surgeon and mates
recruits.role: In battle a fallen man the surgeon reaches in time is wounded, not killed.
recruits.description: A surgeon with his instruments and two mates.

recruits.name: King's colour party
recruits.role: Carries the colours in battle: squads near them rally in half the time; if they fall the whole side feels it.
recruits.description: An ensign and sergeants with the King's colour.

recruits.name: Drums
recruits.role: Signals in battle: an order carries on through them, and line infantry near them load in cadence.

recruits.name: Regimental surgeon
recruits.role: In battle a fallen man the surgeon reaches in time is wounded, not killed.
recruits.description: The regimental surgeon and his mate.

recruits.name: Gun crew
recruits.role: Serves one field gun. An army with a crew, standing in a town you hold, takes a gun laid up in that town's magazine and brings it to its battles.
recruits.description: Four men drilled to a gun, raised where a Workshop can make them rammers, sponges and cartridges. A crew with no gun fights as infantry.

recruits.name: Royal Artillery detachment
recruits.role: Serves one field gun. An army with a crew, standing in a town its side holds, takes a gun laid up in that town's magazine and brings it to its battles.
recruits.description: A detachment of the Royal Regiment of Artillery.
